questions.q: In the self-service password reset example, what does Engage do first?
options: Captures the request and makes sure the real underlying need — fewer routine service desk calls — is understood and relayed with context
Builds the self-service tool directly
Decides the organization's overall budget priorities
Writes the final test plan for the rollout
questions.explain: Engage is the entry point — it captures and relays stakeholder needs accurately, rather than building or prioritizing anything itself.

questions.q: What does ITIL 4 call a specific combination of value chain activities and practices assembled for a particular scenario?
options: A service value system
A value stream
A guiding principle
A service level agreement
questions.explain: A value stream is exactly this: a tailored combination of activities, practices, and resources for one specific scenario.

questions.q: Why might a single user calling in to use an already-built self-service password reset be a much smaller value stream than building that capability in the first place?
options: Because Deliver & support is not actually involved in resolving the call
Because Plan must approve every individual phone call
Because Engage and Deliver & support do almost all the work, with Plan, Design & transition, and Obtain/build barely involved since the capability already exists
Because value streams are always exactly the same size regardless of scenario
questions.explain: Once a capability exists, using it is a small value stream dominated by Engage and Deliver & support, unlike building it in the first place.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where might Improve realistically surface an opportunity during this example?
options: Only after the entire value chain has fully completed and the request is archived
Only inside the Continual Improvement practice, never inside any other activity
Only during Plan, since Improve cannot act during any other activity
At any stage — Engage noticing a repeating request pattern, Design & transition noticing a repeated defect category, or Deliver & support noticing the live tool needs a fix
questions.explain: Improve runs continuously inside every other activity, not as a separate stage that only fires at one fixed point.

questions.q: Why does Chapter 4 start with Incident Management, according to this lesson?
options: Because that's where most of the day-to-day practice work in ITIL 4 actually happens, at the Deliver & support stage of the value chain
Because Incident Management replaces the need for a Service Value Chain entirely
Because Plan and Engage are no longer relevant after Chapter 3
Because Design & transition and Obtain/build are deprecated practices
questions.explain: Deliver & support is the continuous, operational activity most practices in Chapters 4 and 5 live inside, starting with Incident Management.
